newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico says lower interest rates needed.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico says lower interest rates needed.

text.p: Mexico needs lower interest rates in order to consolidate its economic recovery, Banco de Mexico said in its six-month report on the economy.
"In order to consolidate the economic revocery, it is indispensable that real and nominal interest rates maintain their downward trend," Banco de Mexico said in the report released on Monday.
The central bank said that an expansionary monetary policy was not the answer for creating lower interest rates.

"In reality, the opposite would come about," it said. "The public knows that an expansionary monetary policy would lead immediately to a higher exchange rate and then later to (higher) prices," it said.
The central bank reiterated that both exchange rate and interest rates have been determined by market forces.
It said during the year, interest rates have adjusted to new information more so than the exchange rate.
It said that this was the result of the fact that the high interest rates at the start of the year reflected expectations of an important depreciation of the currency.
When this did not pan out, exchange rate depreciation expectations adjusted downwards, which contributed to lower inflationary expectations and then to lower interest rates.
The central bank added that the government reduced its fiscal demands for credit, which also eased pressures on interest rates.
The central bank added that it did not "have the intention of defending a particular level for the exchange rate or interest rates."

"A renewed confidence in the economic program as well as (better) perspectives on the economy, have permitted, despite temporary fluctuations, interest rates to drop markedly in respect to the levels that they reached at the end of last year," it said.
Banco de Mexico noted that short-term foreign investment in peso denominated instruments fell throughout 1995 and 1996 to a relatively modest level at present.
The central bank said that savings rates in Mexico needed to grow, and infrastructure needed to be better developed.
It said that while significant advances have been made in the economic recovery, "this does not mean that the crisis has been overcome."
The central bank reiterated that the primary aim of its monetary policy has been to combat inflation.
It noted that the evolution of the monetary base during 1996 has been along its expected path.
